input: Get a tetanus booster shot this month

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether they have a primary care doctor or prefer a walk-in clinic/pharmacy determines where they should go and how much scheduling effort is involved.
Whether they have health insurance — and what it covers — affects cost, provider choice, and urgency of finding a low-cost option.
Knowing if they have their vaccination records tells us whether they need to retrieve records first before a provider can confirm the booster is due.
Tetanus boosters come as Td (tetanus + diphtheria) or Tdap (adds pertussis); the right formulation depends on their last shot type and age, which changes what they ask for.
If this is for themselves vs. arranging it for a dependent (child, elderly parent) the steps, providers, and consent requirements differ significantly.
Understanding what is blocking them right now (fear of needles, forgetting to book, not knowing where to go) shapes which part of the plan needs the most support.
Some people want to get this done in one errand (pharmacy, no appointment); others prefer their own doctor for continuity of care — this changes the recommended next action.

gold.taskTitle: Get a tetanus booster shot this month
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to obtain a tetanus booster (Td or Tdap) vaccination within the current month.

questions.title: Do you have a regular doctor or prefer a walk-in?
questions.description: Identifies the care setting — primary care provider, urgent care, or retail pharmacy — which determines the scheduling path.

questions.title: Does your insurance cover preventive vaccinations?
questions.description: Determines out-of-pocket cost and which providers are in-network, affecting where to book.

questions.title: Do you know when you last had a tetanus shot?
questions.description: Establishes whether vaccination records need to be tracked down before booking, and confirms the booster is actually due.

questions.title: Do you need Td or Tdap (the whooping cough version)?
questions.description: Clarifies which formulation to request, since Tdap is recommended if the last shot was Td and pertussis protection is needed.

questions.title: Is this shot for yourself or someone you care for?
questions.description: Determines whether consent, guardianship, or age-specific provider requirements come into play.

questions.title: What is the main thing stopping you from booking right now?
questions.description: Surfaces the real blocker — anxiety, time, information gap — so the plan can directly address it.

questions.title: Do you prefer a quick pharmacy visit or a scheduled appointment?
questions.description: Guides the recommended next-action format — walk-in retail clinic vs. booked appointment — based on the user's convenience preference.
